anchor: IGH_locus
notes: 14q32.33. The primary anchor of this panel. Partners run from the canonical five to a long tail of published rare partners and to partners not yet described, so a dictionary of named pairs cannot cover it. Report any IGH junction whatever the partner, including an off-panel partner resolving only to a cytoband.

anchor: IGK_locus
notes: 2p11.2. Light-chain enhancer hijack. Rarer than IGH but the same argument applies.

anchor: IGL_locus/IGLL5
notes: 22q11.22. Light-chain enhancer hijack. IGL::MYC is the best described, but the anchor is not restricted to it.

anchor: MYC
notes: 8q24.21. Both Ig and non-Ig donors, and the described partner list is long and still growing (Barwick 2019 reports partners across many loci in CoMMpass). MYC rearrangement is a progression event rather than a defining one, so the tier comes from the dictionary and this anchor only ensures the junction is surfaced.

anchor: # dist_policy
# body      the breakend must lie inside the named gene body, or the label
#           must be a named interval with no body to measure from. This is
#           the safe default: a panel interval is wider than the gene it is
#           named after, so a breakend merely inside the interval is not
#           evidence about the gene.
# interval  the anchor fires anywhere its label applies, including the
#           flank. Every anchor on this panel is set to interval, and the
#           reason is the panel's design rather than laxity: these windows
#           are deliberately wide because the breakpoints are dispersed.
#           t(11;14) breakpoints sit 100-400 kb centromeric of CCND1, MYC
#           breakpoints scatter over megabases, and t(14;16) breakpoints sit
#           in WWOX intron 8 about 5 Mb from MAF. Requiring the breakend to
#           be in the gene body would discard exactly the events the BCR
#           windows were added to capture, which is the failure the v1 panel
#           already demonstrated.
#           The distance is not discarded. gene_a_dist and gene_b_dist carry
#           it on every row, so a reader can see how far a breakend sits
#           from the gene it was named after and judge accordingly.
# partner_policy
# any       fires whatever the partner is. A self-pair never fires: an
#           anchor is a claim about partners, and a locus joined to itself
#           has none. Without that guard every V(D)J and somatic
#           hypermutation product inside IGH, IGK and IGL would inherit
#           reportability from a rule that was never about them, and those
#           recombine physiologically in a plasma cell neoplasm.
# self      fires only on an intragenic event. Not used on this panel.
